references.text: Proverbs describes the righteous as an everlasting foundation, in contrast to the wicked who perish—the same image of a solid foundation that Luke uses.
Isaiah speaks of a cornerstone, a tested stone laid in Zion as a sure foundation. The image of building on the rock in Luke corresponds with this promise of a secure foundation.
Matthew's parallel account of the wise man who built his house on the rock and the foolish man who built it on sand. This is the direct parallel to Luke 6:47-49 in the Sermon on the Mount.
Jesus says he will build his church on this rock, and the gates of Hades shall not overcome it—a related image of building on an unshakable rock.

Paul speaks of laying a foundation as a skilled master builder, and that no one can lay any other foundation than the one already laid, Jesus Christ. The image of building on the right foundation parallels Luke 6:48.

Believers are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, with Christ Jesus himself as the cornerstone. The whole building is joined together and grows into a holy temple—the same theme of building on a firm foundation.
Peter writes about Jesus as the living stone and believers as living stones being built up into a spiritual house, referencing the precious cornerstone in Zion.
The Lord is my rock, my fortress, and my deliverer—a foundational image in the Psalms of God as the solid rock upon which one can build their life.
Moses' song praises God as the Rock whose works are perfect. The image of God as a rock forms the background for Jesus' parable about building on the rock.

Those who trust in the Lord are like the mountains of Zion, which do not shake but stand firm forever. The image of stability and an unshakable foundation parallels the house that withstands the flood in Luke 6:48.
